global.h3: Long-range strikes kill nine as Russia and Ukraine escalate
global.summary: Overnight missile and drone barrages killed at least five people in Russia and four in Ukraine as both sides widened attacks on rear-area targets.
body: A Ukrainian drone hit a warehouse in the Moscow region on Tuesday, killing five people and wounding ten, according to regional governor Andrei Vorobyov, while Kyiv said its forces struck logistics hubs and oil infrastructure deep inside Russia. A Russian strike on a fuel station in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast killed three people including a rescue worker and his young son.

The exchanges follow a record July in which Russia fired 381 missiles at Ukraine, the highest monthly total of the war. Analysts say Moscow's spring-summer offensive has failed to deliver significant territorial gains more than two months in.

global.h3: Netanyahu refuses Gaza pullback until Hamas fully disarms
global.summary: The Israeli prime minister rejected parts of a US-brokered plan, saying troops will hold current lines until Hamas hands over its weapons.
body: Benjamin Netanyahu pushed back Tuesday on a disarmament framework announced by President Donald Trump that would see Hamas surrender its arms while Israel withdraws and gradually transfers authority to a Palestinian administration. The terms drew a cool response across Israeli politics and media.
Netanyahu said Israel would not leave its positions before disarmament is complete, casting doubt on the timeline for any handover of power in the enclave.

global.h3: Israeli strikes kill Gaza civilians as monitors urge de-escalation
global.summary: The Board of Peace criticised continued Israeli bombardment that has killed civilians and destroyed medical supplies since a disarmament deal was announced.
body: Board of Peace representative Nickolay Mladenov said two days of strikes across Gaza had killed civilians and wrecked medical stocks people rely on. At least 19 Palestinians were reported killed in a single day, part of a weekend toll of 26.
The bombardment continued even as the agreement announced by Washington called for de-escalation, deepening doubts about whether the ceasefire framework can hold.

global.h3: China holds live-fire drills as Taiwan tests wartime resilience
global.summary: Beijing staged exercises in the Taiwan Strait while Taipei ran annual drills rehearsing how the island would keep fighting and communicating under attack.
body: Beijing launched a two-day live-fire drill after President Lai Ching-te said Taiwan was not subordinate to the People's Republic of China, a remark China branded reckless and provocative. The exercises added to a stretch of heightened military pressure around the island.

During its own drills Taiwan tested relocating weapons production lines and converting civilian factories for military use, and for the first time deliberately slowed mobile internet to simulate scarce bandwidth during an invasion.

global.h3: Russia set new July record for missile barrages on Ukraine
global.summary: Moscow fired 381 missiles during July, the highest monthly total and daily rate since the full-scale invasion began.
body: Russian forces launched an average of just over twelve missiles a day in July, setting wartime records for both scale and pace, according to Ukrainian military figures. Air defences were stretched as cities across the country came under repeated fire.
Despite the intensified bombardment, analysts say Russia's ground offensive has failed to produce operationally significant gains more than two and a half months after it began.

global.h3: Trump says Iran talks resume as Hormuz deal edges closer
global.summary: The president confirmed negotiations were restarting and aides said an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could land within days.
body: Trump said talks with Iran were resuming and warned Tehran it faced a final chance to reach a deal on the strait and its nuclear programme. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said an agreement to restore free movement through the waterway could be reached within a day or two, a step that could ease energy prices.
The president also lashed out at Iranian leaders as duplicitous, accusing them of seeking meetings while publicly denying any direct contact.

global.h3: Iran denies direct US talks, points to Oman shipping deal
global.summary: Tehran said it was not negotiating with Washington but was working with Oman on a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz.
body: Iranian officials rejected Trump's claim of active negotiations, saying discussions were limited to Oman over a corridor for shipping through the strait. Tehran has insisted on keeping a role in managing passage through the strategic route, while Washington demands unrestricted navigation.
The competing accounts left the status of any deal unclear even as US officials suggested a breakthrough was imminent.

global.h3: US 35 percent tariff on Canada takes effect
global.summary: A new 35 percent duty on Canadian goods came into force on August 1, escalating trade friction between the neighbours.
body: The tariff followed Trump's July threat and adds to a wider 2026 trade regime that sets a 10 percent base reciprocal rate for most countries and higher tiers for a list of 46 economies including China and Vietnam. Ottawa has warned of countermeasures.
Washington also declined to renew the USMCA at its joint review, leaving the pact in force with zero-percent preferences but shifting it to annual reviews and a possible 2036 sunset.

global.h3: EU wins US ceiling as 15 percent trade deal beds in
global.summary: A transatlantic accord that took effect July 1 caps most EU-origin goods at an all-inclusive 15 percent rate.
body: The deal replaces the base reciprocal tariff layer for the bloc with a single 15 percent ceiling on most exports to the United States, giving European exporters more certainty after months of uncertainty. Brussels framed it as a way to shield industry from steeper duties.
The arrangement sits alongside a patchwork of country deals Washington has struck as it reshapes global trade under a reciprocal tariff model.

global.h3: EU ministers back Spain in Schengen clash with Italy
global.summary: Home affairs ministers sought to calm a solidarity crisis after Italy imposed checks on arrivals from Spain following a mass crossing at Ceuta.
body: More than 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta around July 30, and Rome responded by reintroducing checks on non-EU arrivals from Spain by air and sea, the first time a state invoked Schengen powers against a country it does not border. Ministers meeting by video conference sided with Madrid to defuse the row.
The standoff exposed deep strains over migration burden-sharing as arrivals surged on the western Mediterranean route.

global.h3: Guinea-Bissau under military rule after disputed vote
global.summary: The armed forces seized power following a contested presidential election whose results were never released.
body: General Horta Inta-a Na Man is serving as president after the military took control in the wake of a race between incumbent Umaro Sissoco Embalo and challenger Fernando Dias da Costa. Authorities have set December 2026 as a target for fresh elections.
The takeover adds to a run of military interventions across West Africa, where entrenched incumbents and youth frustration continue to strain fragile democracies.

global.h3: Nearly 19.5 million in Sudan face acute hunger
global.summary: UN analysis warns two in five Sudanese are in crisis-level food insecurity as the civil war grinds into a fourth year.
body: More than five million people face emergency hunger and around 135,000 are living in catastrophic conditions, according to the latest assessment, while over 825,000 children risk death from severe malnutrition this year. Close to nine million people have been displaced inside the country.
Aid access is crippled by the destruction of markets, clinics and water systems, with about 40 percent of health facilities non-functional and 17 million people lacking safe drinking water.

global.h3: South Sudan hunger crisis pushes 7.8 million to the brink
global.summary: Intensifying fighting has driven millions into high acute food insecurity, with 2.2 million children acutely malnourished.
body: UN agencies say 7.8 million people face high levels of acute food insecurity, and nearly 700,000 severely wasted children are at grave risk of dying. Aid officials have warned the country could tip into full-scale famine if violence keeps blocking relief.
The deterioration compounds a regional emergency spilling across borders as conflict in neighbouring Sudan displaces families and disrupts harvests.

global.h3: US wildfires burn 4.5 million acres in record season
global.summary: More than 42,000 fires have scorched over 4.5 million acres this year, well above the ten-year average.
body: The season has run at 130 percent of the average number of fires and 146 percent of average acres burned, with blazes reported from Louisiana to South Dakota. Officials warn compounding heat and drought are stretching firefighting resources thin.
The United States is one front in a global fire year that has also hit Europe and South America hard.

global.h3: European wildfires char more than 250,000 hectares
global.summary: Over a quarter of a million hectares have burned across Europe this year amid record heat and drought.
body: More than 1,250 fires have been detected since the start of 2026, with southern Europe bearing the brunt of a punishing summer. In Chile more than 3,000 wildfires were recorded in the 2025-2026 season, underscoring a worldwide surge.
Scientists link the intensity of the blazes to persistent heatwaves that have dried out vegetation and lowered river levels across the continent.

global.h3: Texas hit by second 1,000-year flood in two years
global.summary: Parts of Texas are reeling from flash flooding after another extreme rainfall event, the state's second such deluge since 2024.
body: The downpour triggered dangerous flash floods and rescues as forecasters described a 1,000-year rainfall event, a marker of how sharply extreme precipitation has intensified. Communities were still assessing damage as the water receded.
The flooding is part of what analysts have called a summer of compounding disasters, with fires, floods and record heat striking in overlapping waves.

global.h3: UN warns climate alarm is blaring from every direction
global.summary: The UN's climate chief said human and economic costs are reaching national emergency levels as another heat surge builds.
body: Simon Stiell said the mercury was set to soar again as fires, floods and heat converged worldwide, calling the mounting damage a crisis reaching emergency proportions. He urged governments to accelerate action ahead of the next round of climate talks.
His warning came as danger-season indicators tripled compared with earlier baselines, with scientists pointing to a cascade of extreme events across the northern hemisphere summer.

global.h3: At least 72 dead in mass crossing to Spanish Ceuta
global.summary: A surge of more than 60,000 people from Morocco toward the enclave of Ceuta left dozens dead in late July.
body: The crossing around July 30 overwhelmed the tiny North African enclave and set off an EU political crisis over how to share responsibility for arrivals. Rescue and medical services struggled to cope with the scale of the movement.
The tragedy sharpened debate over migration on the western Mediterranean route and strained relations between Madrid, Rabat and other EU capitals.

netherlands.h3: Jetten races to break nitrogen deadlock and free up building
netherlands.summary: The prime minister says the Netherlands must end its nitrogen impasse fast to restart stalled permits for housing, farming and roads.
body: Rob Jetten has made clearing the nitrogen logjam a priority, arguing that frozen permits are choking home construction and infrastructure. The plan targets up to 46 percent lower agricultural emissions and 50 percent cuts from mobility and industry by 2035, with 20 billion euros set aside to support farmers and restore nature.
The push carries political risk as ministers weigh how hard to press cuts without reigniting the farmer protests that shook earlier governments.

netherlands.h3: Jetten government moves to tighten asylum rules
netherlands.summary: Ministers are drawing up fresh asylum restrictions after the Senate blocked an earlier bill to harden the system.
body: Asylum minister Bart van den Brink wants to broaden the definition of undesirable aliens to target people who resist deportation, offered as an alternative to criminalising illegal residence outright. The move follows Jetten's pledge to produce new measures within weeks.
The centrist coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is trying to show it can manage migration without the hardline tone of the previous cabinet.

netherlands.h3: Local objections stall power grid expansion amid congestion
netherlands.summary: Community resistance is delaying grid upgrades even as the Netherlands struggles with severe network congestion.
body: Efforts to expand the electricity network are running into local objections that hold up new lines and substations, worsening a capacity crunch that has left businesses waiting for connections. Grid operators warn the bottlenecks threaten housing and industrial projects.
The delays highlight the tension between the energy transition and the not-in-my-backyard resistance that slows big infrastructure work.

netherlands.h3: Working past 67 becomes standard in Dutch labour deals
netherlands.summary: New collective agreements increasingly treat employment beyond the state pension age of 67 as normal.
body: Labour deals are shifting to make working past 67 a standard option rather than an exception, reflecting tight labour markets and an ageing workforce. Employers and unions are building in arrangements for older staff who want to stay on.
The change points to a gradual rethink of retirement as the Netherlands grapples with worker shortages across sectors.

netherlands.h3: New law forces makers to repair appliances after warranty
netherlands.summary: Manufacturers will be required to fix broken appliances even once the warranty has expired under a new Dutch rule.
body: The measure obliges producers to repair faulty appliances beyond the warranty period, part of a broader right-to-repair push aimed at cutting electronic waste. Consumer advocates say it should extend the life of everyday devices.
It lands as the EU rolls out wider repair and sustainability rules that reshape how products are sold and serviced.

netherlands.h3: Dutch inflation climbs to 3.1 percent in July
netherlands.summary: A CBS flash estimate put July inflation at 3.1 percent, up from 2.9 percent in June.
body: Statistics Netherlands said consumer prices rose 1.6 percent in July from June, lifting the annual rate to 3.1 percent. The EU-harmonised measure came in at 2.9 percent, also higher than the previous month.
The uptick keeps price pressures above the European Central Bank's comfort zone, with full CPI figures due on August 11.

netherlands.h3: DNB expects house price growth to cool to 3 to 4 percent
netherlands.summary: The central bank forecasts annual house price rises of 3 to 4 percent through 2028, sharply below recent years.
body: De Nederlandsche Bank said falling consumer confidence and rising mortgage rates are leaving buyers both less willing and less able to borrow, easing the pace of price growth. More homes are also coming to market as ex-rental properties are sold off.
The slowdown offers modest relief in a market long defined by shortages and steep price gains, though affordability remains stretched in the big cities.

netherlands.h3: Dutch unemployment edges up as growth stays modest
netherlands.summary: CBS counted 393,000 unemployed in early August as forecasts point to a slowly rising jobless rate.
body: The number of unemployed reached 393,000, with economists expecting the rate to climb toward 4.2 percent this year and 4.4 percent in 2027. Growth is projected around 1 percent to 1.2 percent, held back by capacity bottlenecks.
Fitch reaffirmed the Netherlands' AAA rating with a stable outlook, citing strong institutions and eurozone membership.

netherlands.h3: Shell sells European onshore renewables to TotalEnergies
netherlands.summary: Shell agreed to offload its European onshore renewable energy operations to rival TotalEnergies.
body: The deal hands TotalEnergies Shell's onshore wind and solar assets across Europe as the Anglo-Dutch major continues to trim its renewables footprint and refocus on core businesses. It marks another step in Shell's retreat from parts of the green portfolio it built up in recent years.
The sale underscores shifting strategies among oil majors weighing returns from renewables against traditional energy.

netherlands.h3: Wildfire risk in the Netherlands nearly doubles in a decade
netherlands.summary: New analysis finds the country's wildfire danger has roughly doubled over the past ten years amid hotter, drier summers.
body: The KNMI produced a wildfire impact forecast for the first time this year as fire services warned of rising danger across heath and forest. The finding lands during a parched summer that has left vegetation tinder-dry.
Officials say the trend reflects a warming climate that is reshaping risk in a country better known for water management than drought.

netherlands.h3: Fast-moving Limburg wildfire proves hard to extinguish
netherlands.summary: A rapidly spreading blaze in Limburg is expected to take a long time to bring fully under control.
body: Fire crews battled a fast-moving wildfire in Limburg that officials warned could smoulder for an extended period given dry conditions. The fire added to mounting concern about drought-driven blazes this summer.
Elsewhere, low water levels forced several ferries in Gelderland out of service as rivers ran exceptionally low.

netherlands.h3: Drought deficit nears the record set in 1976
netherlands.summary: The precipitation shortfall has reached 250 millimetres, closing in on the country's worst dry spell on record.
body: A second dry spring in a row has pushed the rainfall deficit toward the 1976 benchmark, leaving rivers low and water stress rising. The southeast has seen the fourth heatwave of the year, with local highs around 33 degrees.
Water authorities are managing shipping and irrigation as the parched conditions ripple across agriculture and inland transport.

netherlands.h3: Home visits by Dutch family doctors fall 50 percent
netherlands.summary: House calls by GPs have halved over the past 15 years as primary care shifts away from home visits.
body: The number of home visits by family doctors has dropped by half in a decade and a half, reflecting workload pressures and changing practice models. Patient groups worry the trend leaves frail and elderly people with less at-home care.
The finding feeds a broader debate about strain on Dutch primary care and access for those who cannot easily travel to a surgery.

netherlands.h3: WorldPride fills Amsterdam through early August
netherlands.summary: Amsterdam is hosting WorldPride from late July into August, a global celebration of LGBTQIA+ rights and visibility.
body: The two-week festival running to August 8 has drawn crowds and events across the city as Amsterdam takes its turn hosting the international Pride gathering. Organisers framed it as a show of solidarity and visibility at a time of political pushback in some countries.
The celebration coincides with a busy summer cultural calendar in the capital, from comedy to community festivals.

netherlands.h3: EU AI Act's next stage brings content labelling rules
netherlands.summary: A new phase of the EU AI Act took effect on August 2, requiring firms to label content mainly generated by AI.
body: Under the second stage of the bloc's landmark AI law, companies including those in the Netherlands must flag content primarily created with artificial intelligence. The rollout marks the world's first comprehensive legal framework for the technology.
Businesses are adjusting compliance as obligations phase in, part of a wider push to bring transparency to AI-generated media.

mood.p: Nederland wordt vandaag wakker in een broeierige, kurkdroge zomer, met veel zon en temperaturen die in het zuidoosten oplopen tot boven de 30 graden. Het neerslagtekort nadert het record van 1976, rivieren staan laag en de brandweer waarschuwt voor natuurbranden na de snel om zich heen grijpende brand in Limburg. Tegelijk hangt er een feestelijke stemming in Amsterdam, waar WorldPride de stad kleurt en de vakantie langzaam ten einde loopt.
